ranked.precision_gap: Baseline persistent original/master owner shards are FP32; gathered compute weights and source-rank duplicate-coalesced dense embedding gradients are BF16, then cross-rank reduction and microbatch accumulation are FP32. Automodel BF16 owner parameters use ordinary BF16 parameter gradients and would demote persistent owner storage/accumulation relative to baseline. Selecting FP32 owner storage matches the baseline persistent master dtype, but ordinary FP32 F.embedding changes compute/output dtype and owner-side duplicate coalescing compared with the baseline per-source BF16 coalescing boundary. Merely casting lookup output to BF16 does not establish backward parity. Ignored parameters do not inherit FSDP FP32 reduction/accumulation. Adaptation is required.
ranked.compile_and_SAC: Exact-count mode reads count metadata to host. Default strict_validation documents about twenty device-host synchronizations and seven small collectives per lookup; disabling strict validation retains one count-matrix read. Opt-in capacity_mode calibrates once at max first-lookup count times 1.25 then rejects overflow. Official Qwen model guide keeps owner-collective block eager and outside activation checkpoint recomputation; no fullgraph compile/SAC readiness established.

tests.lines: 320-340 exact local FP32 F.embedding values/gradients; 343-409 two-rank CPU/gloo distributed values, summed gradients, and one SGD update, including duplicate rows and empty requester

Hopper_evidence.qwen_lines: 44-69: 64/128 row owners, 8 nodes/64 H100 baseline, 100 steps, finite training/validation and full distributed checkpoint; 164-177: owner block not checkpointed, MTP unsupported
Hopper_evidence.deepseek_conditions: Guide lines 148-192 identifies 100-update H100 validation at e2c47c5b with torch 2.13/NCCL 2.30.5 and owner128/owner64 configurations, BF16 gradients/moments and no or little accumulation, specific network-plugin/PXN workarounds. This is actual owner-path validation, not only build support; it is not a benchmark of [128256,4096], DP8, acc32, GFSDP, EMA or MTP1.

occurrence_routing_detail.deduplication: None. Stable sort groups every token occurrence by owner. Both forward values and reverse gradients are per occurrence. Owner F.embedding backward coalesces duplicates after reverse all-to-all.
occurrence_routing_detail.metadata: AllGather P int64 counts into P-by-P count matrix. Exact-count path reads matrix to host; payload still uses equal-split global-maximum padding. Capacity mode calibrates first maximum times1.25 aligned64 and asserts overflow later.
occurrence_routing_detail.performance_risk: With raw language token IDs, balanced request distribution is not established. One hot requester-owner pair increases every padded segment. Deduplication and a workload-safe count/capacity schedule need consideration; first-batch capacity is not a general bound.

ranked.facts: Native sparse=True embedding gradients enter SparseTensor and sparse_allreduce gathers row indices and values with padded all_gather, then returns COO gradients. Current config.py explicitly rejects removed sparse_gradients flag (dense-gradient compression removed). engine.py:3144-3168 routes ZeRO>=2 through partition epilogue and ZeRO1 through optimizer.reduce_gradients rather than sparse fallback. Sparse engine gather is not a ready ZeRO/GFSDP row reduce-scatter replacement, and AdamW sparse-gradient handling needs densification/custom optimizer seam.
ranked.Hopper: No matching Hopper embedding-gradient benchmark identified.

ranked.facts: Maintained recommendation framework and TensorFlow custom-op embedding integration, not a maintained PyTorch/GFSDP input embedding replacement. SOK optimizer dump/load documentation explicitly says Adam behaves as LazyAdam, not TensorFlow Adam. HugeCTR Global update exists and updates all rows, so it should not be mischaracterized as all sparse-only updates; still no ready dense AdamW/EMA/GFSDP integration.
ranked.Hopper: H100 examples/build support and HPS inference numbers are not row-gradient training measurements. Official open issue 482 reports obsolete SOK benchmark APIs on H20 Hopper; no matching H100/H200 LLM training benchmark found. HPS and embedding cache, not SOK itself, deprecated since 25.03.

exclusions.facts: allreduce_sparse is conditional on IS_NCCLX; ordinary NCCL errors. NCCLX allocates dense output. Crucially sparse API is not sparse-wire transport.
exclusions.ncclx_facts: Lines 91-111 describe memset dense receive buffer, unpack sparse blocks, ordinary dense allreduce. Explicitly warns sparse input causes significant padding data exchange. Meta NCCLX is not an NVIDIA sparse collective product.

exclusions.facts: TP vocabulary mask then local dense embedding and allreduce/reduce-scatter embedding outputs. Assumes aligned TP token requests; distinct DP rank requests need explicit routing. No drop-in row-only DP gradient communication.

OmniReduce exposes research sparse collectives with RDMA/DPDK aggregation infrastructure, not ready maintained GFSDP integration. Pici paper reports adaptive sparse reduce-scatter/allreduce but no inspected maintained LLM integration or matching Hopper workload was established. Do not use paper maximum speedups as prediction.

Newer PyTorch/TorchRec sequence-mode dynamic embedding supports BF16 and row routing, with actual H100 NVSwitch and Eos IB benchmarks. README:230-232 lists separation of backward and optimizer update as future work. APIs:804-807 limits non-rowwise-Adagrad optimizer states to embedding dtype, so BF16 Adam moments differ from FP32 baseline. Fused optimizer path is not an external dense AdamW once-per-acc32 update seam. D4096 support was not established in bounded inspection; benchmark D128 and BF16 256-byte rows cannot establish it.

verification: Official source code and documentation inspected at listed revisions. No benchmarks, installs, test execution, or source edits performed.
coordinator_reconciliation: Local contract is the authority for baseline persistent FP32 shards versus BF16 compute replicas. Prefer initial backward-only row exchange selecting already-coalesced native BF16 rows, widening each contribution before owner FP32 SUM, and retaining existing dense local gradients/AdamW/EMA/checkpoint ownership. Reuse Automodel routing/all-to-all concepts, not its numerical/optimizer path unchanged.
